FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( S~ec ond Revision the draft finalized by the Rolling Bearings Mechanical Engineering Division Council. ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after Sectional Committee had been approved by the Light

The standard IS 7461 on General plan of boundary dimensions for tapered roller bearings was first published in 1974 and was revised in 1980 to align with IS0 355 : 1977 `Rolling bearings - Metric roller bearings - Boundary dimensions and series designation' in regard to the tapered international practice followed for the designation of tapered roller bearings. tapered roller bearing -Double row Subsequently Addendum 1 to IS0 355 : 1977 `Metric dimensions' and Addendum 2 to IS0 355 : 1977 `Metric tapered roller bearings -Boundary were issued in 1980. The subjects of these bearings - Flanged cups - Boundary dimensions' amendments were not covered in the Indian Standard. Therefore, the revision of IS 7461 : 1980 has been taken up and following three standards have been brought out to cover the entire subject given in IS0 355 : 1977, Addendum 1 to IS0 355 : 1977 and Addendum 2 to IS0 355 : 1977. GENERAL PLAN OF BOUNDARY DIMENSIONS FOR TAPERED ROLLER BEARINGS
PART 1 SINGLE ROW BEARINGS ( 1 SCOPE This standard (Part 1) covers general plan of bounda;y dimensions for single row metric tapered roller bearings. 1 .I This standard also specifies the series designation of each bearing. 2 TERMINOLOGY 2.1 Angle Series Represented a range of contact angles of tapered rollers for a given diameter series and width series and is identified by numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7. 2.2 Diameter Series

Second Revision )

Represents a range of values for the outside diameter to bore relationship and is identified by alphabet A, B, C, E, F and G. 2.3 Width Series Represents a range of values for the width to section height relationship and is identified by alphabet A, B, C, D and E. 2.4 Dimensions Series A combination of angle series, diameter series and width series. 3 NOTATIONS Notations, represent standard. 4 SERIES as shown in Fig. 1 shall Abe used to various dimensions as used in this DESIGNATION shall be referred to dimension

%mdard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products~are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ,Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Zndian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises eon the basis of comments. Standards are any reviewed periodically: a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards Monthly Additions'.
